cls: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor (irreversible ErbB-family / EGFR inhibitor)
pharm: Covalently and irreversibly binds the kinase domains of EGFR (ErbB1), HER2 (ErbB2), and HER4 (ErbB4), inhibiting autophosphorylation and downregulating ErbB signaling that drives tumor cell proliferation
quick: 40 mg orally once daily until progression or intolerance (30 mg in severe renal impairment)
Take at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal (food reduces exposure)
Can cause fetal harm; use effective contraception
Reduce to 30 mg once daily in severe renal impairment (eGFR 15-29)
No starting-dose adjustment for mild-moderate; monitor liver tests; not studied in severe
Diarrhea/hydration, skin, liver tests, pulmonary symptoms, eyes
summary: Afatinib dimaleate (Gilotrif) is an irreversible ErbB-family (EGFR/HER2/HER4) tyrosine kinase inhibitor indicated for first-line treatment of metastatic NSCLC with non-resistant EGFR mutations and for metastatic squamous NSCLC progressing after platinum-based chemotherapy. The recommended dose is 40 mg orally once daily on an empty stomach. Key toxicities are diarrhea (can cause dehydration/renal failure), skin reactions, ILD, hepatotoxicity, GI perforation, and keratitis, managed by dose interruption/reduction.
indications: First-line treatment of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with non-resistant EGFR mutations detected by an FDA-approved test
Treatment of metastatic squamous NSCLC progressing after platinum-based chemotherapy

dosage.t: Once daily until disease progression or no longer tolerated
dosage.n: Take at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal
AUC ~50% higher in severe renal impairment

dosage.c: Adult - dose modification for adverse reactions
dosage.d: Withhold; resume at 10 mg/day less than the dose at which the reaction occurred once resolved/baseline/Grade 1
dosage.n: Permanently discontinue for life-threatening skin reactions, ILD, severe hepatotoxicity, GI perforation, persistent ulcerative keratitis, symptomatic LV dysfunction

dosage.d: Reduce by 10 mg/day with P-gp inhibitors if not tolerated; increase by 10 mg/day with chronic P-gp inducers as tolerated
dosage.n: Return to prior dose when the interacting drug is stopped

admin: Take orally once daily at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal
Select patients for first-line use based on a non-resistant EGFR mutation by an FDA-approved test
Do not take a missed dose within 12 hours of the next dose
Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
Dispense in the original container to protect from humidity and light
moa: Afatinib covalently binds to the kinase domains of EGFR (ErbB1), HER2 (ErbB2), and HER4 (ErbB4) and irreversibly inhibits tyrosine kinase autophosphorylation, resulting in downregulation of ErbB signaling. Certain non-resistant EGFR kinase-domain mutations (most commonly exon 21 L858R substitutions and exon 19 deletions) cause increased receptor activation that supports NSCLC cell proliferation; afatinib inhibits this autophosphorylation and proliferation.

relative: Pre-existing severe diarrhea risk, significant hepatic dysfunction, interstitial lung disease, or active corneal disease (heightened toxicity risk)
monitor: Diarrhea severity and hydration / renal function
Skin (bullous/exfoliative reactions), liver function tests, pulmonary symptoms, ocular symptoms

preg: Based on animal findings and its mechanism of action, afatinib can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman; there are no human data. In rabbits it caused embryotoxicity and increased late abortions at maternally toxic doses; in rats it caused skeletal alterations and reduced fetal weight. Advise pregnant women of the potential risk and advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment.
lact: There are no data on the presence of afatinib in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant or milk production; afatinib was present in the milk of lactating rats. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment.
renal: No starting-dose adjustment is needed for mild to moderate renal impairment. For severe renal impairment (eGFR 15 to 29 mL/min/1.73 m2), reduce the dose to 30 mg once daily, as exposure (AUC) was about 50% higher.
hepatic: No starting-dose adjustment is recommended for mild (Child-Pugh A) or moderate (Child-Pugh B) hepatic impairment; afatinib has not been studied in severe (Child-Pugh C) impairment. Monitor liver function periodically, and withhold or discontinue for severe or worsening liver tests.

moderate: P-glycoprotein inhibitors (ritonavir, cyclosporine, ketoconazole, itraconazole, erythromycin, verapamil, quinidine, tacrolimus, nelfinavir, saquinavir, amiodarone) - increase afatinib exposure; reduce dose by 10 mg/day if not tolerated
Chronic P-glycoprotein inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, St. John's wort) - decrease afatinib exposure; increase dose by 10 mg/day as tolerated
interactions.food: A high-fat meal decreases Cmax by ~50% and AUC by ~39%; take at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal
interactions.diagnostics: Requires an FDA-approved EGFR mutation test for first-line patient selection; monitor liver tests

serious: Severe diarrhea with dehydration and renal impairment (some fatal)
Bullous, blistering, and exfoliative skin disorders
emergency: Acute or worsening interstitial lung disease
Severe dehydration / acute renal failure from diarrhea

monitoring: Bowel movements / diarrhea severity, hydration status, and renal function
Skin for bullous or exfoliative reactions
EGFR mutation status (FDA-approved test) before first-line use
counsel: Take once daily on an empty stomach - at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after eating
Start anti-diarrheal medicine at the first sign of loose stools and stay well hydrated; report severe or prolonged diarrhea
Report skin blistering or peeling, new or worsening cough or breathlessness, eye pain or vision changes, and severe abdominal pain
Use effective contraception; this medicine can harm an unborn baby, and do not breastfeed
Do not take a missed dose within 12 hours of the next dose
pk: Steady-state plasma concentrations reached within about 8 days of repeat dosing
Tmax 2 to 5 hours; relative bioavailability of tablet ~92% versus oral solution
Once-daily dosing; eliminated primarily in feces (~85%)
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); keep in original container, protect from humidity and light
pearls: Irreversible pan-ErbB inhibitor for EGFR mutation-positive (exon 19 deletion, L858R) NSCLC; not effective against resistant EGFR mutations
Diarrhea is near-universal and can cause dehydration and renal failure - start loperamide early and dose-reduce/withhold for severe cases
Take on an empty stomach; high-fat food markedly reduces absorption
Watch for ILD, hepatotoxicity, GI perforation, and keratitis - several require permanent discontinuation
Adjust dose for P-gp inhibitors/inducers (decrease 10 mg with inhibitors, increase 10 mg with inducers)
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered, but do not take a missed dose within 12 hours of the next scheduled dose - skip it and resume the normal once-daily schedule.
overdose: Reported overdose (360 mg as part of a mixed-drug ingestion in two adolescents) caused nausea, vomiting, asthenia, dizziness, headache, abdominal pain, and mildly elevated amylase; both recovered. There is no specific antidote; provide supportive care and monitor for the known toxicities (especially diarrhea, dehydration, and GI effects).
